question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=4{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=$ {{field-1}},
$\,{X}_{2}(s)=$ {{field-2}}.
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}L\{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)\}=L\{-{x}_{1}(t)\} \\ L\{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)\}=L\{4{x}_{1}(t)+2{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}sL\{{x}_{1}(t)\}-{x}_{1}(0)=-L\{{x}_{1}(t)\} \\ sL\{{x}_{2}(t)\}-{x}_{2}(0)=4L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}+2L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+1=-{X}_{1}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-3=4{X}_{1}(s)+2{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L\{{x}_{1}(t)\}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L\{{x}_{2}(t)\}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
s{X}_{1}(s)+1=-{X}_{1}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{1}(s)=-\frac{1}{s+1}.
$$

Substituting this in the second equation and solving for ${X}_{2}(s),$ we have

$$
s{X}_{2}(s)-3=4(-\frac{1}{s+1})+2{X}_{2}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{3s-1}{(s+1)(s-2)}.
$$
